channel.title: Buenos Aires Times – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Buenos Aires Times – Bias and Credibility (batimes.com.ar)

item.title: Videla’s confession: Reconstructing the dictatorship
item.description: Published in 2012, 'Disposición Final' features an extended interview with military junta leader and former de facto president Jorge Rafael Videla. To mark the 50th anniversary of the coup d’état that brought him to power, we run a translated extract from Ceferino Reato’s historic non-fiction book.

item.title: 50 tales for 50 years: Book collects personal stories of dictatorship’s crimes
item.description: 'La Retaguardia,' media outlet specialising in coverage of trials probing crimes against humanity during the military dictatorship, has compiled accounts drawn from court files and testimonies given in court.

item.title: Football and memory: the dictatorship’s shadow on the game
item.description: Fifty years after the 1976 coup, the sport continues a long struggle to uncover the fate of the disappeared.

item.title: The 24th of March
item.description: Over the years, I have learned that – for the most part – those who reach the Presidency and lead Argentina do not possess superior virtue. They are just as flawed as the average person.

item.title: EU-Mercosur trade deal to apply provisionally from May 1
item.description: EU authorities say sweeping free-trade agreement with South America's Mercosur bloc will provisionally enter into force on May 1; Pending court ruling could still throw spanner in the works.

item.title: Survivors recall horror of dictatorship, 50 years on from coup
item.description: Survivors of Argentina's 1976–1983 dictatorship are representatives of a decimated generation whose stories of torture, death and exile are coming back to life, 50 years after the coup.

item.title: Voices from the darkness: 20 dictatorship survivors and their tales
item.description: Half a century after the coup, a look at 20 key survivors who not only lived through the terror, but helped the country understand what happened and prosecute those responsible.

item.title: Paris campus steps in after Argentine residence removes dictatorship plaque
item.description: Paris university campus to install dictatorship victims plaque after dispute; Cité Internationale Universitaire will install its own memorial amid concerns over politics and neutrality at Maison de l’Argentine.

item.title: Argentina remembers painful legacy of dictatorship as Milei challenges narrative
item.description: Human rights groups to lead commemorations as Milei government questions long-standing narratives about dictatorship's crimes; Political battle grows over how nation remembers military regime and victims.

item.title: Milei government calls for ‘complete history’ of dictatorship era in video
item.description: La Libertad Avanza restates its position on the 50th anniversary of Argentina’s 1976 coup, highlighting left-wing violence; Seventy-five minute video features interview with recovered granddaughter and son of a former soldier kidnapped by guerrillas.
